::: {.callout-note}
## D4 at a glance

- **Discrimination:** held-out AUC {{< var score.auc_holdout >}} on the held-out
  {{< var score.test_share >}} of applicants (bootstrap 95% interval
  {{< var score.auc_ci_lo >}}–{{< var score.auc_ci_hi >}}).
- **Gate:** AUC ≥ {{< var score.gate >}} on that population, asserted at training and
  recomputed by `verify.py` — met.
- **On the loans the bank books:** held-out AUC {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the
  {{< var score.pop.booked.n >}} booked applicants in the held-out split — below the gate value.
- **Six open findings** the chapter raises about its own model ([4.7](limitations.qmd)).
:::

The Business Credit Score is a weight-of-evidence scorecard: {{< var score.n_features >}}
features, each binned and replaced by its bin's weight of evidence, combined by a logistic
regression and scaled to a score between `SCORE_MIN` and `SCORE_MAX`
([4.1](purpose.qmd)). It is the platform's score spine: every other
model and the pricing engine consume its output ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd)), which makes
it Tier 1 ([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#risk-tiering)).

This chapter is the worked example of the nine-part [template](../index.qmd#the-template).
Every number in it is a named fact, recomputed through the modules' own functions by
`python verify.py` — the stress refits in [4.6](sensitivity.qmd) only under
`python verify.py --full`; the [fact index](../../reference/facts.qmd) gives each one's
source and population.
